objectives: Measure short /o/ recognition, decoding, spelling and comprehension separately.
Check accuracy of short /o/ CVC reading and encoding.
Identify component-specific errors for targeted remediation.
Use accurate rereading as an early fluency measure.
concepts: Diagnostic assessment should isolate component skills.
Accuracy precedes speed in early phonics fluency.
Error patterns determine the next instructional response.

definitions.definition: An assessment used to identify strengths and specific learning needs.
Accurate and increasingly automatic reading of taught material.
A specific part of phonics performance such as sound recognition, decoding or encoding.

workedExamples: hot read as hat → inspect the middle vowel.
dog read as dag → check o versus a.
Accurate but slow reading → use repeated accurate rereading rather than sacrificing accuracy.
commonMistakes: Treating every error as a decoding problem.
Using only a total score without component analysis.
Advancing without checking the diagnosed gap.

basic: Complete short /o/ recognition and decoding checks.
application: Read and spell taught short /o/ words.
higherOrderThinking: Choose the next instructional step from an error pattern.
mixedReview: Combine recognition, decoding, encoding and comprehension.

mistakeBasedRevision: o/a confusion → vowel discrimination and mapping.
slow accurate reading → repeated accurate rereading.
weakTopicRevision: Practise the exact weak component before reassessment.

activities.name: Fluency reread
steps: Observe increasing smoothness without reducing accuracy.

outcomes: Learner demonstrates at least 80% accuracy on short /o/ recognition and decoding checks.
Learner demonstrates at least 80% accuracy on short /o/ spelling checks.
Learner answers controlled-text comprehension questions with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner uses accurate rereading to support developing fluency.
Teacher can identify the component skill requiring remediation.
